heading: INT. GREENHOUSE AT A DEFUNCTIONING ORCHID BREEDER'S - NIGHT

units.text: INT. GREENHOUSE AT A DEFUNCTIONING ORCHID BREEDER'S - NIGHT
Steam clings to the glass like breath on a window.
Rows of orchids glow under purple grow lamps, their petals speckled like skin, and the air is warm enough to loosen a collar.
A long potting table has been set for a dinner nobody quite wanted: four chipped plates, a bottle of wine, a bowl of lemons.
ISOLDE FAIRWEATHER, thirty-five, the breeder, in a canvas apron over a silk dress, pours wine with the steadiness of someone holding her hand still on purpose.
Across from her, THEODORE "TEDDY" NAKAMURA, thirty-eight, who once loved her and has returned to buy the business, loosens his tie and looks everywhere but at her.
At the end of the table sits PERPETUA OYELARAN, seventy, Isolde's aunt, picking a lemon apart with her fingernails.
Beside her, his phone face-down by his plate, is ANTON LUNDGREN, forty, Isolde's fiancé, who has just realized who Teddy is.
You flew eleven hours to look at flowers.
units.name: ISOLDE

units.text: I flew eleven hours for the Phalaenopsis line. The flowers are incidental.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: She doesn't sell the line.
units.name: ANTON

units.text: Everything's for sale at the right hour of the night, Anton.
units.name: PERPETUA

units.text: Aunt Perpetua.
units.name: ISOLDE

units.text: She isn't wrong.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: You two have history. Say it. I'd rather hear it than guess it.
units.name: ANTON

units.text: Anton, not here.
units.name: ISOLDE

units.text: I'd say here's the best place. Nothing here can hear but the orchids.
units.name: PERPETUA

units.text: We were engaged. For nine months. It ended before you met her.
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: She told me it was a boy she knew at school.
units.name: ANTON

units.text: It was easier.
units.name: ISOLDE

units.text: It always is.
units.name: PERPETUA

units.text: Isolde, I'm not here to cause --
units.name: TEDDY

units.text: Then why are you here, Teddy? Honestly. Why is there a man at my table who knows which side of the bed she sleeps on?
units.name: ANTON

units.text: That's enough!
units.name: ISOLDE

units.text: Left. She sleeps on the left.
units.name: PERPETUA

units.text: Perpetua!
units.name: ANTON

units.text: Isolde stands.
The bottle tips and wine runs across the table toward the lemons.

Teddy reaches to catch it at the same moment Anton shoves his chair back, and the two men collide at the corner of the table, the chair crashing into a rack of seedlings, Perpetua calmly lifting her plate out of the flood and Isolde pressing both palms to her face.
Then, in the quiet of the falling trays, a single orchid stem snaps.
That one was nine years old.
units.name: ISOLDE
